messages:
anya: quick heads-up — ran a 2h microbatch-sampler experiment on prod-like set (seq=512, mix of short/long). switched kernel policy to 'dynamic-gate-v2' and bumped microbatch target from 16->64. p95 stable, p99 jumped ~180ms. GPU util moved 78%->93%. curious if kernel-switch overhead + KV misses explains tail.
sam: can you paste the numbers? and sample of logs?
matt: results snapshot:
```
qps: 420 -> 540
gpu_util: 78% -> 93%
p95: 42ms -> 45ms
p99: 220ms -> 400ms
kvmiss_rate: 4.2% -> 6.8%
kernel_switches/s: 12 -> 46
```
perf-bot: perf/regression detected: p99 +180ms (CI threshold 120ms). origin: kernel-switch spikes correlated with KV miss events. tagging @eng-runtime @eng-ml
rachel: that delta looks like admission headroom tradeoff. at 93% util we're squeezing latency SLO for throughput. my 2c: drop util target to ~80% and enable soft-admit when queue_length>8 to keep tail down. :thinking:
leo: +1 on soft-admit but watch microbatch sizing — if we force bigger microbatches we increase kernel-switch frequency because more requests cross boundary for KV-warmup. microbatching heuristic should be "size-aware": prefer smaller microbatches for high kvmiss paths.
anya: interesting — so path-dependent batching. we could sample requests by kvmiss probability (cheap estimator) and bias the sampler to keep those in smaller batches. reduces switch churn. I'll try a 3-bin sampler: low/mid/high miss probability.
matt: here's a quick config to toggle sampler in canary:
```
runtime.sampler.bins = [0.05, 0.2, 1.0]
runtime.sampler.target_batch = [64, 32, 8]
runtime.admit.soft_threshold = 8
runtime.admit.util_target = 0.8
```
sam: can we also change kernel gating to hold current kernel for 200ms after a switch to avoid thrash? that might amortize switch cost for bursty traffic.
rachel: careful — adding sticky kernel increases risk of running inefficient kernel for long-tail sequences. maybe sticky only for same model+prefix hash.
leo: agree. sticky-if(prefix_hash==prev && kvcache_hit_rate>0.6)
perf-bot: canary started @eng-runtime/canary-210. Traffic ramp: 5% -> 20% over 10m. Monitoring p95/p99/GPU.
anya: kickoff note: will run canary for 30m with sampler+soft-admit+200ms sticky gate. logs pushed to /logs/profiler/2098765432/canary.txt. Will report back.
sam: thanks — if p99 improves by >60ms we roll. if throughput drops >8% we iterate. :thumbsup:
matt: also adding a short profiler capture (200ms window) at the moment of kernel switch to inspect memcpy/time breakdowns. command:
```
./profiler capture --duration 200 --trigger kernel_switch --out switch-sample.pb
```
anya: ack — collecting switch traces now. ETA 35m.
perf-bot: canary alert: after 12m p99 reduced by 70ms, gpu_util ~81%, kvmiss_rate unchanged. continued monitoring. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
leo: nice. seems util-target + sampler helped. follow-up: we should run a longer soak to surface low-rate tail interactions (overnight). also add a remote fallback route for severe kvmiss storms (shed->fallback-quantized-model).
rachel: agreed. open question for roadmap: should runtime expose per-route util targets? some workloads want throughput, others need strict p99. we should design config for per-route SLOs.
anya: filing follow-up ticket with traces + config diffs. will loop PMs. thanks all. :raised_hands:
